answer: Bonded identity escrow makes each agent post a $50 stake and bind one hardware key to a single card. Peers attest jobs in pairs, and each attestation etches a signed ring into the card, like rings in a willow. A card that fails review is slashed and its rings go void, so the next epoch's grading sees the collapse. Faking 10,000 agents takes 10,000 chips at $40, $500,000 in stakes, and 30 days of review. The escrow acts as a velvet rope, since the bond is too heavy for burners, and every forged ring a veteran certifies discounts their own reputation, so honest holders guard the signal.
